# Frontend Route Audit

**Generated by:** `node scripts/route-audit.mjs`
**Commit:** see git history — rerun the script rather than trusting this snapshot.

Phase 1 of `REFOCUS.md`. Answers three questions per route: can a user reach it,
does it look like a real screen, and what backend surface it depends on.

## Method and its limits

Static analysis of `frontend/app`, `frontend/components`, `frontend/lib`. It
parses `href=`, `href={...}`, template-literal hrefs, `router.push/replace` and
`redirect()` targets, then matches them against the app-router page tree
(dynamic segments collapse, so `/x/${id}/edit` matches `/x/[id]/edit`).

**It cannot prove a route renders.** It does not run the app, log in, or hit the
API. Flags are leads to verify, not verdicts. Two flags are especially noisy:

- `no-fetch` — no literal `/api/...` string in the route's own files. Server
  components, shared `lib/api` helpers and hooks all fetch without one, so this
  means "no *direct* call here", not "no data".
- `ORPHAN` — no in-app link. Correct for dead features, wrong for routes entered
  from outside the app (email links, public shares). Both cases are below and
  they are labelled.

## Headline

| | |
|---|---|
| Routes | 73 |
| Exposed in `AppShell` nav | 21 |
| Orphaned (no in-app link) | 9 — 6 real, 3 expected |
| Stubs (≤30 LOC of feature code) | 3 |

**73 routes, 21 reachable from the nav.** That is the "features unavailable
because of bad design" complaint, quantified: two thirds of the app is reachable
only by already knowing the URL, or by finding a link buried inside another
feature.

## Orphans that are real bugs

| Route | LOC | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `/trainers/my-trainer` | 245 | **The trainer feature you are keeping cannot be reached.** Nav has `/trainers` (browse); nothing links to the screen showing the trainer you actually have. |
| `/trainers/requests` | 173 | Same feature, same problem. Pending trainer requests are invisible unless you type the URL. |
| `/admin/moderation` | 108 | Content-report queue, calls `admin` endpoints, unlinked from `/admin`. |
| `/admin/recipes` | 136 | Unlinked from the admin index. |
| `/admin/relationships` | 192 | Unlinked, and carries a `TODO`. |
| `/community` | 6 | A stub that was never finished or removed. |

`/trainers/my-trainer` and `/trainers/requests` are the finding that justifies
rev 2's thesis. Those screens are built, wired to `Trainers` endpoints, and
unusable — not because the feature is bad, but because nothing links to it.
Deleting trainers would have thrown away working code to fix a missing `<Link>`.

## Orphans that are correct

Entered from outside the app; no in-app link is the right design.

| Route | Entered from |
|---|---|
| `/reset-password` | password-reset email |
| `/verifyemail` | verification email |
| `/u/share` | public share link |

## Stubs

| Route | LOC | Call |
|---|---|---|
| `/community` | 6 | delete |
| `/trainer/clients/[id]` | 21 | finish — it is the trainer-side client detail view, and the trainer product needs it |
| `/admin/ingredients/add` | 30 | thin wrapper, fine as is |

## Actions for phase 3

1. Link `/trainers/my-trainer` and `/trainers/requests` from `/trainers`, and
   surface "my trainer" as a tier-2 contextual strip when a relationship exists.
2. Link `/admin/moderation`, `/admin/recipes`, `/admin/relationships` from the
   admin index, or drop them into the MCP admin tools per REFOCUS §8.
3. Delete `/community`.
4. Finish or delete `/trainer/clients/[id]`.
5. Audit the 5 routes carrying `TODO`/`FIXME`: `/admin`, `/admin/users/[id]`,
   `/admin/relationships`, `/ai`, `/profile/settings`, `/trainers/my-trainer`.
